The measured signal exceeded the five-standard-deviation threshold expected for a background-only hypothesis, and the cross-section for top quark events was calculated at 57.2 femtobarns with an uncertainty of ±5.2 femtobarns, which aligns with predictions from quantum chromodynamics models.

This study focuses on key elements in cross-domain text-to-SQL parsing, specifically schema linking and value filling. To enhance encoding abilities, a column selection auxiliary task is proposed, leveraging explicit targets for relevance matching. Additionally, two value filling approaches are presented to bridge the gap between current zero-shot parsers and practical applications, considering that many existing parsers overlook value filling in synthesized SQL. Experiments on the Spider dataset demonstrate the superiority of our proposed framework over baseline models through two main criteria evaluation.

The ongoing LoTSS survey is conducting a deep radio sky survey at 144 MHz with a goal to identify galaxy distribution characteristics in European skies. Our analysis utilizes a large sample of galaxies within the southern hemisphere skies European flux limited catalog in the LoTSS DR1 dataset. Specifically, a catalog containing 6404 galaxies within J2000 coordinates between 4 and 6 hours RA and -14 and -12.5 degrees declination with redshift estimates > 0.4 based on existing literature. This research computes a power spectrum and galaxy bias within the identified galaxy sample. Furthermore, the study compares its findings with previous studies and theoretical models, particularly those related to the matter bias factor in the context of a specific cosmological model.

The High-Dimensional Rank Lasso (HDR Lasso) model offers a comprehensive solution for a wide range of high-dimensional regression challenges, especially those difficult to manage due to numerous variables. Despite its applicability, the problem associated with HDR Lasso is computationally intensive and requires extensive computation due to its non-smooth, non-differentiable, and piecewise linear characteristics, making existing computation methods inefficient for handling numerous variables. This research introduces a novel Computation Efficient HDR Lasso (CEDHL) algorithm to address this challenge by applying lie algebra concepts to optimize the algorithm. Building upon rankless optimization principles and leveraging adaptive techniques to accelerate convergence, the proposed algorithm effectively tackles HDR Lasso by reducing its associated Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions to a Markov decision process problem, which can be efficiently resolved through iterative forward/backward pruning techniques. The algorithm has been tested and validated on synthetic and real-world data, demonstrating significant improvements, such as reduced execution time and increased accuracy, compared to existing solutions, such as the Optimal Lasso Algorithm and a Optimized Lasso Algorithm for Regret.

Identifying whether an optimal solution is localized or universal is particularly challenging in complex optimization problems. This work addresses that challenge by demonstrating the existence of a single, optimal, and universal method for achieving the lowest possible rate of entropy production in fast and sluggish driving processes. This outcome stems from the fact that the entropy production rate can be expressed as the sum of separate, independent terms, each corresponding to a distinct current-pair. Building on this discovery, the article describes the essential attributes of these currents under relaxed constraints, which facilitate the location of optimal solutions in more intricate and complicated scenarios.

Over the past decade, significant advancements in AI have been made in numerous domains. Concurrently, the environmental consequences of AI solutions such as autonomous vehicles and energy consumption prediction systems have begun to gain attention. Despite the positive environmental applications of AI, the environmental impacts of developing these solutions remain largely overlooked in both AI research and sustainability studies. To rectify this, we initially employ a straightforward method to quantify the environmental effects of creating AI models, showcasing how training large models exacerbates greenhouse gas emissions. Subsequently, we utilize a comprehensive framework derived from supply chain research to map out and evaluate the environmental consequences of the AI development process. Our model incorporates four primary categories of environmental resources, namely human-generated carbon emissions, water consumption, electricity consumption, and raw material extraction. We identify and quantify various environmental drivers, including AI development team sizes, infrastructure energy sources, and local cost of capital. Our research reveals that an AI development project akin to GPT-3 could result in the loss of 400 times more water than is consumed in producing a single iPhone, translating to approximately 400,000 liters of water, equivalent to 130,000 liters of water for 320 new iPhones. Our model also indicates that the environmental costs associated with training large AI models may be 50 times greater than anticipated in previous studies. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the environmental impacts of an AI development project extending over 3 years could be equivalent to those of constructing

This paper investigates and classifies various prescriptive process monitoring methods, which identify potential issues during business processes and provide interventions to prevent problems at the point of occurrence. Our systematic review initially presents an definition of prescriptive process monitoring along with its associated challenges, a comprehensive bibliography of relevant studies, a detailed analysis of various monitoring approaches, their applications, and potential use cases. Furthermore, our analysis highlights the current state of research in this field, suggesting several directions for future investigation.

A generalized Boussinesq model has been developed to simulate complex material processing flows, incorporating the effects of convection and diffusion as well as coupling between stress and anisotropic strain hardening. The presented research introduces an error estimation method based on the residual that measures the error of specific integral quantities in a fluid dynamics system resulting from the lack of exact solution. Unlike traditional a priori approaches, the novel a posteriori method utilizes discrepancies between the residual and a measure of local data oscillation, offering error evaluation after computations have occurred. The research presents three specific objectives: estimating the total energy in the system, an average temperature in a designated area, and the maximum temperature at a selected point. The accuracy of the proposed approach has been validated through its successful application in two benchmark problems involving the mixing of materials and the solidification of materials.

Polynomial-time reduction methods, referred to as kernelization algorithms, decrease the size of problems for specific algorithmic issues called packing problems. These problems include diverse challenges such as finding independent sets and matching within graphs, and address more fundamental questions in computer science. Although determining the independence number of a graph remains a central theoretical question, these problems can be resolved efficiently under specific constraints on the input data. Researchers have developed kernelization algorithms for packing problems under a specific parameter, combining the packings' sizes and relevant graph attributes. Specifically, these kernels depend on both variables, resulting in uneven distribution across related algorithms. Our research presents new linear-sized kernels for 2-dimensional matching and square-free triangle-free graphs, achieving a significant improvement over existing techniques. However, we also demonstrate that some packing problems cannot be reduced linearly under simultaneous consideration of multiple variables.

This study explores how opinions are shaped and social connections evolve in a complex system, governed by a delicate balance between friendly and hostile relationships. We have developed a model that simultaneously considers the tendency for like-minded individuals to group together and their preferences to associate with diverse others. Our simulations reveal that these dual influences often result in multiple distinct social clusters, each characterized by a unique set of opinions. Moreover, we have found that small variations in a parameter can cause significant shifts in the number of these clusters. At the individual level, we have observed that people within the same cluster tend to hold similar views, while connections between clusters are influenced by individual characteristics.

We've investigated a newly constructed series of asymptotically flat, electrically charged black holes that form scalar "hair" when their charge increases beyond a certain point at any given mass. Inside the event horizon, these black holes resemble a holographic superconducting material, exhibiting similar behavior in their scalar fields and culminating in a singularity that closely mirrors the interior of a Reissner-Nordström black hole. Our analysis reveals areas of unusual features where the scalar field stabilizes and displays a flat profile. Furthermore, we observe that in certain regions, as one approaches the central singularity, the behavior of the scalar field is directly influenced earlier on, from outside the black hole, by variations in the dimension parameter, particularly when these variations result in change of sign.

Different genes exhibit varying levels of transcription delay, and the factors contributing to this delay across the entire genome are still not well understood. The entire process of RNA production, encompassing transcription, nuclear export, and RNA maturation, can cause delays that vary across the genome and have implications for the overall length of RNA produced. By integrating existing experimental data on these processes, we developed a comprehensive model of RNA production that accurately replicates the overall delay observed in cells, and we identified the specific contributions of each cell process and mRNA decay to this delay. Analysis of genomic features revealed that the density of transcription start sites and transcription speed are major drivers of overall transcription delay, and that genes with higher expression levels and longer lengths experience additional delays due to increased transcription and elongation rates, and that genes with longer lengths experience delays resulting from increased transcription and elongation rates. The findings indicate that delay models can provide a framework for studying gene regulation and that features influencing these delays may provide clues about the functional attributes of genes, and that genes with delayed RNA production are more likely to be associated with diseases.

Recent studies of high-energy particle collisions with the TRIPLE-Dirac method have revealed unusual low-energy configurations within the nickel-64 nucleus, specifically cases with no rotational angular momentum but distinct internal structures. Our calculations using the large-scale shell-model approach revealed a crucial role of the monopole tensor interaction in shaping these unusual configurations, coupled with specific particle arrangements involving $0f_{5/2}$ states near the Fermi level. Furthermore, our advanced three-body model incorporating the monopole tensor force accurately reproduced the experimentally measured energies of several low-lying excited states, including some with angular momentum, thus validating our theoretical framework.

Chiral SU(N) gauge theories, consisting of Weyl fermions and additional fermions, are examined to analyze their dynamics. An older suggestion by Bars and Yankielowicz to match the theory's 't Hooft anomalies with those of free fermions is revisited, resulting in additional constraints for the fermion content. Using 't Hooft's consistency conditions, I demonstrate that, similar to their supersymmetric counterparts, some chiral theories spontaneously break the symmetry. Furthermore, I examine possible dualities within these theories. Specifically, I prove that SU(2) gauge theories, with specific Fermi mode representations, do not achieve duality. Conversely, I establish that supersymmetric theories' duality is unique, and duality may also apply to related QCD theories.

A linear complementary pair of group codes $(C, D)$ is formed when the direct sum of $C$ and $D$ results in the entire group algebra $R[G]$, given a finite principal ideal ring $R$ and a finite group $G$. We identify a required and confirming criterion for pairs of group codes $(C, D)$ in group algebra $R[G]$ to be a linear complementary pair, subsequently proving the equivalence in terms of permutations between codes $C$ and the dual code $D^{\perp}$.

We introduce a new approach to representing functions in graphical models that capitalizes on sparse dependencies. This novel approach simplifies the computation of joint probabilities and wields two significant advantages: it expedites Most Probable Explanation (MPE) significantly, and enables feasible constrained optimisation where previously it was infeasible. To this end, we also present a novel algorithm for tackling constrained optimisation issues in graphical models.

The visual appearance and accompanying audio cues can be effectively combined to locate hidden objects within an image. Our proposed method leverages the inherent audio-visual relationship through an asynchronous processing framework. Initially, we extract distinct features from audio and visual inputs separately, then synthesize them into a unified feature set, ultimately inputting it into a classification system. Notably, our technique does not depend on pre-identified sound patterns or visual cues associated with specific target objects. Through comprehensive evaluations on real-world datasets related to object detection, we demonstrate substantial improvements over methods employing audio-visual integration as well as vision-based approaches alone. Our results indicate that audio-visual fusion yields more accurate results than vision-based methods alone, highlighting the significance of integrating multimodal data for complex detection tasks.

When subjected to high rates of deformation, many dense mixtures and granular materials suddenly become stiff and sticky. Despite being well-known for decades, the underlying stark contrast in their behavior remains poorly understood. Researchers investigated the universal aspects of this phenomenon by closely controlling the composition of thick suspensions consisting of hard particles. Through controlled experiments, researchers discovered that all transitions followed a identical pattern regardless of the specific parameters, characterized by distinct exponents. Furthermore, data collected from various testing methods overlapped perfectly when specific variables were combined. theoretical modeling suggested that a single frictionless structure explains both the sharp transition in material stiffness and the abrupt change in viscosity.

This study investigates the fluctuating electricity consumption in Ghana's period of power shortages by applying a traditional time series analysis and a cutting-edge deep learning model known as LSTM. The analysis involves hourly data collected over a year, specifically from January to December 2017. Two approaches are employed in addressing the challenge, specifically the ARIMA and LSTM models. The results indicate that these models accurately forecasted electricity usage during periods of power shortages, with a mean absolute percentage error rate lower compared to other models in literature. ARIMA and LSTM models consistently resulted in an MAPE rate of 5.66% and 2.26%, respectively, when analyzing hindcasted data, and 3.76% and 2.36%, respectively in examining the forecasted data. Consequently, it was concluded that the LSTM model exceeded its counterpart in terms of accuracy in capturing hourly patterns of electricity consumption during power shortages.

An increasing number of Web search users rely on personalisation to tailor search results to their individual profiles. Despite its popularity, there have been no in-depth user studies examining the influence of personalisation on search users. Our research investigated this phenomenon using a controlled user study with 100 participants in Switzerland, comparing how many users found relevant information through Web search with and without the effect of personalisation. Our study revealed that search users may miss significant amounts of relevant information as a direct consequence of their previous search activity. Additionally, users who discover information through their search queries tend to engage with that content more deeply. Our findings also indicated that personalisation has a more pronounced effect on less experienced users. These users tend to personalise their browsing activity more heavily. Moreover, users who discover information through their search queries personalise more heavily when it is disabled.

Automatically creating programs from complex specifications like pseudo-code or flow charts is a program synthesis task, for which multiple approaches have been proposed. Preliminary results on simpler tasks without data-driven components have been achieved, yet these methods struggle to scale effectively. Our proposed solution employs a fully data-driven approach, leveraging neural networks to overcome these limitations. We introduce a new architecture, consisting of a fully connected layer and a graph recognition convolutional neural network, to transform flow charts into programs using two distinct layers to capture the structural features of the input and the transformation process, respectively. Empirical evaluations have been conducted on two tasks, namely graph recognition and program synthesis, with results showing superior performance compared to existing methods, particularly on a newly created flow-chart-based program synthesis dataset.

This text explores multiple reduction techniques that facilitate the connection of Earth's climate models of varying complexity, emphasizing approaches that enable thorough reduction. It distills key mathematical concepts behind each method while showcasing several benchmark climate modeling examples for illustrative purposes.

The employment of laboratory-created ejecta models in modeling kilonova emissions relies heavily on data obtained from high-resolution atomic calculations. This study focuses on refining existing oscillator strength data, particularly for low and middle atomic number elements, in order to enhance the accuracy of these models in capturing the complex spectra generated during supernovae explosions, especially at their early stages. The precise oscillator strengths, conducted at an uncertainty level of 10% for elements Os through Au, are presented in a comprehensive and open format, facilitating integration into ejecta models to produce synthetic spectra in a comprehensive database, available in a research paper. The accuracy of these calculations is confirmed through comparison with observable features in solar spectra, ensuring their reliability in various astrophysical contexts. The accuracy of these calculations is confirmed through comparison with distinct spectral features, especially in the case of Os, where four major low-lying multiplets have been accurately represented in a model that successfully captures the characteristics of a rapid transient phenomenon, in a manner similar to that of a super-Chandrasekhar white dwarf explosion, known as iPTF16guz.

Radiation oncologists' goal is to target tumors accurately while shielding surrounding vital organs, particularly the gastrointestinal (GI) tracts, from radiation. The manual GI tract segmentation process involves a lot of work and uses a lot of time, but deep learning has offered a viable solution to this problem. This article provides an overview of the use of deep learning for deep straight tube learning, ATTM, and geometric tube modeling in the context of the GI tracts.

Compositional data analysis deals with compositional datasets and the methods used to interpret and model such data. These datasets consist of vectors whose components sum to a fixed total, like 1 or 2. The field of co-association has developed several techniques and interpretations for understanding compositional data relationships. One key challenge arises from the limitations of standard statistical and linear algebra methods when applied directly to compositional datasets. For example, traditional distance calculations fail to accurately capture correlations between compositional data points because they ignore the interdependence of their components. Similarly, classical principal component analysis becomes difficult to interpret when applied to compositional data without accounting for its unique characteristics. Applying logarithmic transformations, specifically the "log-sum-transform" (LST), has proven beneficial in these scenarios as it facilitates meaningful interpretation of results in the context of geometric algebra. This study examines the effects of LST on dataset distances and interpretations in comparison to other常用的 transformations, like the log transform, demonstrating that they shift dataset distances while preserving result interpretations in contrast to other常用的 logarithmic transformations. Our findings emphasize that employing LST in comparative datasets enables meaningful component interaction analysis in percentages,总体的增减 (increases or decreases), and relative changes between components in a more accurate and interpretable manner.

Artificial intelligence models, modeled after biological agents, require a precise regulatory mechanism to manage their focus.  We're examining the link between an agent's attention and the information it acquires from the environment to establish a fundamental principle for monitoring its informational impact. Employing a variational method, we've developed an algorithm capable of training neural agents to maximize the information they gather through attentive observations. We've applied this framework to solve sequential decision-making problems and discovered that agents trained using our approach can efficiently balance exploration and exploitation. Furthermore, our results reveal a direct correlation between an agent's attention efficiency and its ability to make informed predictions about the future.

Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are typically trained using gradient descent on large datasets, but this method is inefficient to a degree comparable to human brain learning. In contrast to this traditional approach, our proposed model utilizes a sparse, U-shaped neurobiologically plausible learning rule that requires minimal updates. Our large-scale experiments reveal that this novel training method significantly reduces data requirements by multiple factors, while also matching the performance of the standard supervised RNN training on various tasks. In addition to its efficient learning capabilities, our research demonstrates that the structured connectivity of our model enables more reliable and interpretable connections between cause and effect, a potential benefit that could contribute to developing more trustworthy artificial intelligence systems.

We categorize nilpotent algebras by dimension with a focus on their commutative, commutative nilpotent and anticommutative properties. Our findings reveal the irreducibility of corresponding geometric spaces, allowing us to accurately calculate their dimensions and establish general families of algebras associated with each space. Additionally, we demonstrate how these results contribute to an understanding of the length of anticommutative algebras in further study.

Active Galactic Nuclei possessing powerful radio jets occur throughout various cosmic epochs. Through magnetic interactions within surrounding material, these jets generate energy that fuels electromagnetic emissions and potentially thermal X-rays from the environment. By driving shockwaves, the jets also facilitate the production of relativistic particles that contribute to non-thermal radio and X-ray emissions. Research suggests that the energy output from the shocks can also heat the cosmic microwave background, though the extent of this energy transfer remains unclear. To address this knowledge gap, we developed a comprehensive and adaptable numerical simulation capable of effectively resolving AGN development and the resulting energy transfer processes. Utilizing this CUbA code, we simulated AGN formation at varying redshifts and found notable variations in thermal and cosmic energy outputs depending on environment. Our results indicate that the redshift at which an AGN forms can significantly influence these energy interactions, potentially leading to substantial increases in local thermal radiation following collisions or reductions in the background energy release.

We perform a covariant expansion of the Einstein-Hilbert action in powers of
$1/c^2$, considering a generic spacetime foliation defined by $c$, the speed
of light. We achieve this through the application of a suitable 'pre-non-
relativistic' geometrical parametrization, thereby facilitating an
analytical $1/c^2$ expansion of general relativity. Ultimately, this method
permits an in-depth exploration of the Einstein-Hilbert action expansion up to
its next-to-next-to-leading order.

This study proposes an advanced method for computing image registration transforms based on 3D SP Symmetry, DP Symmetry, SIFT, and image volume characteristics. Our approach leverages the 3D SP Symmetry filter to extract scale and orientation-specific features from image volumes at multiple pyramidal levels. These features are clustered to generate corresponding descriptors, which guide the matching process. We integrate SP Symmetry matches to align bounds, estimate displacements, and utilize SIFT to register remaining features. Finally, we employ a method combining b-splines and SP Symmetry filters to refine registration across the entire image volume. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance of our approach over existing techniques in terms of accuracy, robustness, and speed.

We've analyzed the data from a unique binary star system, SDSS J082239.54+304857.19, observed during a 2020 eclipse, revealing detailed insights into its properties. Our study confirms earlier findings that establish the binary's period at 40.51 hours and classifies it as an eccentric prototype AE Pyg. We've estimated key characteristics, including masses, radii, and minimum mass for one of its stars, utilizing multi-model fitting of light curves obtained from multiple filters. Our analysis indicates that the Hubble Space Telescope observations filter out noise better than ground-based observations, leading to more precise measurements. Our study also detected significant fluctuations in count rates, consistent with broader trends observed during the ground-based observations, across several filters. Our work also addresses past controversies surrounding the star system's distance, while our new photometric data supports earlier estimates at 3.18 kpc. Our analysis also discusses the possibility of unseen third body presence in this star system, based on our wide-angle proper motion studies.

In numerous machine learning tasks, particularly in deep neural networks, global pooling operations like mean/max pooling are extensively utilized due to their efficiency. These operations simplify deep network models, making them more computationally feasible. Despite their widespread adoption, the potential of global pooling layers has not been fully explored. Our research investigates global pooling from a new perspective - optimal transport theory. We demonstrate that global pooling can be viewed as a form of optimal transport cost, and under specific conditions, global pooling is equivalent to optimal transport. Based on this understanding, we propose a global pooling layer that performs optimal transport, and show through extensive experiments that our proposed layer outperforms conventional global pooling in various tasks. Our optimal global pooling layer achieves superior results in image classification, semisupervised learning, semantic segmentation, data augmentation, and graph-based machine learning compared to traditional global pooling.

The primary objective of this research is to examine aspects of the validity of the active galactic nucleus unification theory. Our focus lies on AGN host galaxies using a comprehensive sample consisting of 104 Type AGN, categorized as Seyfert 1, Seyfert 2, and other types. Employing the morphological classification system proposed by Dressler and Schachter, we assess whether Type 1 and Type 2 nuclei appear hosted by galaxies with various ellipticities. Our findings indicate that Seyfert 1 nuclei are predominantly hosted by galaxies with less complexity, whereas the distribution of hosts for Seyfert 2 nuclei shows no notable distinction. Furthermore, statistical analyses using chi-squared tests and polynomial regressions suggest that, although there is some evidence that Type 1 nuclei are hosted by galaxies with less complexity, current datasets are insufficient to conclusively confirm this hypothesis. Our findings also suggest that observational considerations do not fully explain the observed differences between the two Seyfert categories. Consequently, a comprehensive unification theory is required to fully understand the inherent characteristics of these galaxies.

This paper delves into a comprehensive analysis of general rotational surfaces in the 4-dimensional Euclidean space, focusing on flat general rotation surfaces characterized by a 1-type Gauss map. Additionally, it's established that a non-planar, flat general rotation surface with this distinct Gauss map is a Lie group if and only if it's a Clifford torus.

Deep neural network training for semantic segmentation is a particularly difficult task due to its extremely limited, very high-dimensional data. Several approaches aim to improve this process, with many involving additional pre-training on auxiliary tasks like depth estimation. Our study compares self-supervised depth estimation and image classification as pre-training methods for a high-dimensional task (semantic segmentation). We find that self-supervised depth estimation effectively transfers its pre-training to the main task, with our results surpassing those from image classification pre-training in four tested datasets. Additionally, we explore how our approach impacts segmentations in scenarios where class imbalance is addressed using focal loss, with significant differences evident in scenarios with very few samples.

The ability to create complex, engaging stories about the characteristics of time-series data is crucial in various fields. This document introduces TCube, a neural system capable of creating concise, informative stories from different types of time-series data. Unlike existing systems, which are tailored to work with time-series data from specific fields, TCube is adaptable and can create coherent narratives for data from multiple domains. TCure's approach is based on a neural autoregressive model, which generates coherent first-order sentences step-by-step. To create meaningful, informative stories, a combination of a language model and a sequence distribution module is used, which determines how many sentences should be created. A training module is designed to ensure the accuracy and coherence of time-series descriptions, avoiding unnecessary repetition. In experiments involving data from four different domains, TCure demonstrates state-of-the art performance in describing time-series data, surpassing the performance of existing neural systems, including those trained with transfer learning techniques.

The ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) has achieved precise measurements in two areas, namely neutral B meson mixing and CP violation, as well as in rare electroweak processes occurring in suppressed B-meson decays. This study concentrates on recent findings from the ATLAS collaboration, encompassing evaluations of rare occurrences like $B^0_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ and $B^0 \to \mu^+\mu^-$ decays and CP violation in certain decays including $B^0_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$, $B^0 \to \mu^+\mu^-$, and others.
On a Cayley tree, we analyze the Ising model and find novel periodic measures that are linked to index-2 normal subgroups within its group representation.

This study explores the well-posedness of global solutions, dependence on initial conditions, and final states for hyperbolic systems with uniformly coefficient values close to one but possibly infinite coupling. These systems have coefficients that decrease no faster than the reciprocal of the global logarithm's function, with a focus on 1D transport equations and a broader class of hyperbolic systems. Our main contribution is demonstrating that these equations with such time-varying coefficients exhibit a globally well-posed scenario.

This research introduces a novel application of the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network to tackle the challenging task of Japanese word segmentation. Japanese word segmentation poses a significant challenge due to its ambiguous boundaries and large vocabulary. Traditional methods relying on conditional random fields often fail to capture long-term dependencies, which our proposed use of LSTM aims to overcome. Comparative evaluations were conducted both automatically by comparing evaluation scores and manually through human reviews, demonstrating the efficacy of our approach relative to established methods.

On the Stack Overflow platform, users utilize 11,926,354 external connections to share crucial information beyond its boundaries. Although these links have a substantial impact, their repeated dissemination by users presents challenges in monitoring its extent and monitoring the reliability of destination sites. Based on this premise, our research focuses on identifying and analyzing external links consistently shared on Stack Overflow over extended periods. Through this investigation, our key findings indicate that in 2020, a minority of links accounted for the majority of shared content, with the top 1% comprising external connections contributing 41.6% to this total. Furthermore, the top 10,000 most frequently shared links were responsible for 75% of all shared external content within our dataset. We have also discovered notable patterns of users accessing these links and their subsequent contributions to Stack Overflow community.

Galactic rotation curves reveal a pattern of flatness that can be interpreted in two ways: either as evidence of a significant amount of dark matter or as the effects of general relativity at large distances. Historically, researchers initially attributed these findings to dark matter, but a more thorough examination might suggest that modifications to gravitational theory are warranted. This concept gained further support from observations of galaxy clusters, such as those made through weak lensing observations, which suggested the existence of less than expected amounts of dark matter. Furthermore, a hypothetical model of scalar-tensor gravity with a cosmic factor can be proposed that could eliminate the need for dark matter, although this requires significant adjustments to galactic properties. This discrepancy poses a significant challenge to the galaxy diversity problem, particularly considering that a broad range of galactic rotation curve profiles have not been adequately accounted for by current models. These models, including polytropic dark matter halos and isothermal spheres, can effectively describe various profiles such as rising, falling, rising and then flat, and flat rotation curves.

Although climate change is widely accepted, meaningful conversations about it are scarce,
resulting in slow implementation of necessary societal changes to mitigate its effects.
To enhance climate change communication and promote individual actions, we are developing
Climate Chatter, a system outlined in this paper comprising a Knowledge Base of Climate Facts.
The Climate Facts Knowledge Organiization Structure encompasses multiple categories covering
the full spectrum of climate change implications, encompassing connections between climate, human health, food, and more. Within each category, factual statements are annotated with sentiment and structured into a knowledge base. A total of 4,818 facts were manually collected, organized, and annotated. To supplement the climate knowledge base, we gathered data from various sources including a Wikipedia mirror and news articles, and developed a dataset of 2,042,091 sentences. To facilitate climate-related conversations, we created a conversational agent and implemented a reasoning system capable of answering conversational queries concerning climate-related topics.

Clinical symptoms recorded in unstructured doctor's notes lack consistency due to doctors' subjective writing styles, which can vary significantly between different medical institutions and countries, posing a major challenge for automatic symptom event extraction and understanding. Successful extraction relies heavily on annotated training data from the target institution, complicating the adaptation process. Our research focuses on developing an automatic extraction method for symptoms that encompasses this challenge of domain adaptation. We introduce SymEvent DomGen, a system that utilizes an external, loosely-related clinical dataset to improve its performance on a target dataset for symptom extraction. By incorporating this external data, SymEvent DomGen achieves notable results, surpassing the state-of-the-art domainspecific method by 3.16 F1-score points on an adaptation task. To our knowledge, this represents the first instance of using a related but distinct dataset in symptom event extraction and surpasses current techniques in efficiency.

Deep reinforcement learning has emerged as a promising approach for learning autonomous driving skills, largely due to its ability to solve complex decision-making problems in environments with limited knowledge. Our comprehensive review explores the Deep reinforcement learning framework, key learning processes, and potential applications in autonomous vehicle development. We provide an in-depth analysis of the Deep Q-network, policy gradient, and actor-critic algorithms, showcasing their advantages and limitations. Our research indicates that deep reinforcement learning has contributed significantly to solving autonomous driving challenges, despite initially overlooking potential risks during early development. We conclude by discussing potential improvements and future enhancements that could address these concerns, according to the Society of Automotive Engineers standard.

In recent years, AI networks, particularly those inspired by biological neurons, called spiking neural networks (SNNs), are gaining significant attention due to their potential to tackle energy-efficient AI challenges. Researchers have attempted to leverage the inherent randomness of biological neurons, which is typically neglected in current SNN research, to develop more efficient models. Our investigation focuses on whether this randomness can be exploited to create SNNs that are both accurate and energy-efficient. We introduce a novel classification framework, which incorporates a random SNN classifier composed of randomly shaped neurons, using only its output error probability density function for decision-making. Our approach, termed the Accurate Random SNN Classifier, features several notable advantages, including simplicity, generalizability across network configurations, and the ability to provide an estimate of energy consumption after training. Comprehensive simulations validate that the ARSC achieves exceptional classification accuracy (exceeding 99%) and accurately predicts the energy consumption of random SNNs (exceeding 95%), including low-bit precision models, which were trained and optimized for maximum accuracy. Our results indicate that the ARSC not only matches but also surpasses traditional biological neuron models in efficiency, including those based on Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz dynamics and integrated membrane dynamics, by accurately identifying minimum energy-consuming execution paths through its cumulative distribution function.

This research investigates the thermodynamic characteristics of spin-polarized strange quark matter under a strong magnetic field at finite temperature, applying the MIT bag model. Furthermore, we derived the equation of state for spin-polarized strange quark matter in the presence of a strong magnetic field, and subsequently, we examined the structure of spin-polarized strange quark stars across varying temperatures and magnetic fields.

A surge in personal device ownership presents both opportunities and difficulties when trying to leverage unused computational power for collaborative purposes.  Individuals face challenges due to diverse operating systems and varying levels of technical proficiency on their various devices.  This study proposes Pando, a framework allowing individuals to utilize unused computing power in their personal devices through a personal virtual machine powered by a container and a web-based interface.  Furthermore, it demonstrates the efficacy of such a system in enhancing performance and enhancing transparency in machine learning-based recommendation systems by providing reliable parallel processing capabilities and improved debuggability.

A computational method for resolving nonlinear eigenvalue problems is presented, using an approximating function derived from the eigenvalues of a modified eigenproblem equation.  By utilizing a variable sampling process that focuses data collection on the areas most critical to solution resolution, this algorithm efficiently distributes resources. It then employs the collected information to produce approximations for the sought-after eigenvalues and eigenvectors through further processing. Several numerical demonstrations highlight the performance of this solution strategy.

We demonstrate the topological equivalence of all intermediate beta-transformations with a specific type of greedy beta-transformation that incorporates a hole at zero. By employing this equivalence, we obtain a detailed characterization of these transformations, yielding new insights and results in various areas, such as Krieger embeddings, survivor sets, Hausdorff dimensions, bifurcation sets, and badly approximable numbers. We show that certain classes of sets associated with these beta-transformations possess unique properties, specifically that they are winning in Schmidt games and have the countable intersection property.

We've found that gauge theories with $SO(N_{c})$ as a gauge group and matter fields represented as vectors confine, resulting from monopole condensation and the quark bilinear breaking $SU(N_{F})$ chiral symmetry down to $SO(N_{F})$. Our findings derive from an ${\cal N}=1$ supersymmetric theory, specifically with anomaly-mediated supersymmetry breaking.

Machine learning models such as random forests and AdaBoost have proven effective in various applications, but their complex nature makes them difficult to understand. This paper introduces a new approach to dissect the impact of individual features on predictions in tree-based models. This novel method isolates feature effects to eliminate interactions, enabling clearer analysis. It develops dedicated decomposition formulas for each model type and designs tailored explanation curves that reflect feature importance within specific data subsets. Our framework enables precise evaluation of feature importance, attribute selection, calibration checks, and smooth trend identification. Additionally, this new method serves as a potential technique for fully understanding forest-type ensemble models.

In federated learning, multiple parties collaborate on training machine learning models by exchanging gradients, protecting sensitive data and models. The computational processes involved in this collaboration are often seen as opportunities to manipulate these processes and extract confidential information. However, advancements in hardware, such as Trusted Execution Environments, offer a potential solution to mitigate this risk. Our study investigates how to leverage Trusted Execution Environments in federated learning to enhance the security of both data and models. We present Flatee, a system incorporating TEEs into federated learning, alongside a comprehensive analysis of its benefits. Furthermore, we conduct threat model-based attacks on Flatee, demonstrating its resilience against these threats and highlighting its superior performance over systems based on obfuscation techniques.

The embedded systems industry experienced significant advancement due to autonomous driving capabilities, yet many small embedded systems still rely on simplistic automation techniques. These systems face challenges in ensuring accuracy and safety due to complex automation requirements. We aimed to enhance them by developing an automated automated testing framework for autonomous vehicles. Our approach involved extracting driving patterns from simulated environments and verifying their reproduction on actual hardware. We extracted signatures from simulated and real-world datasets and compared them to identify discrepancies, highlighting potential issues. Our proposed method emerged as a novel solution, distinct from traditional automated testing methods. We evaluated the framework by examining public datasets and two custom collections gathered using an autonomous vehicle prototype. The results demonstrated high accuracy, achieving true positive rates as high as 96.7% and 97.5%, and true negative rates as high as 99.2% and 99.5% on our respective datasets.

Containerized application deployment, particularly containerized Docker images, has become a cornerstone of enterprise application development. Enterprise applications rely heavily on system calls from various domains, such as database and certificate management. Enterprise applications face diverse security restrictions on system calls that can impact their functionality and performance. Violating these restrictions can lead to security breaches, forcing organizations to disable security restrictions, defeating the purpose of securing these system calls. To resolve this, we developed Timeloops, an automated learning technique for system call policies using feedback from security violations. Timeloops enhances the precision of policy learning by resolving issues associated with inter-container communication and reduced search spaces through intelligent filtering. To evaluate its effectiveness, we applied Timeloops to 13 microservice architectures based on real-world security violations and found it generates accurate and verified system call policies with higher precision than existing techniques, requiring fewer validation examples to produce these policies.

Advanced techniques for representing complex data involve transforming it into a higher-dimensional space using linear models and applying standard linear classifiers that yield superior outcomes with reduced training requirements. This research explores space partitioning properties of two high-dimensional classifiers, margin classifiers and maximum margin classifiers, when applied to random data distributed across a binary product structure. It demonstrates that margin classifiers produce linear separators at a distance from the origin proportional to $\Omega(\log n/d)$ in the original space, a property that holds significantly better than random classifiers, which produce margins of $\Omega(\log(1/\delta)/d)$. Moreover, maximum margin classifiers achieve a margin marginally better than random classifiers at a distance of $\Omega(\log(1/\delta)/d)$. For a wide range of parameters, both classifiers produce significantly more complex separators than expected in the original space. Additionally, research into the margin stability and covering properties of these models reveals that, when applied to data drawn from a low-dimensional manifold, these models exhibit stability and cover the space efficiently with an expected number of labels of order $\log(1/\delta)$.

This introduction focuses on stochastic Model Predictive Control methods that account for uncertainty in constraints, illustrated through a linear system under unpredictable conditions. The corresponding Matlab code is also accessible online for reference purposes.

This paper delves into the domain of Unsupervised Learning, introducing a novel compression paradigm for Independent Component Analysis (ICA). A key challenge in ICA is the computational expense associated with producing a high-quality model from extensive datasets. Existing ICA models rely on samples for efficiency; however, they fail to address the scenario where data samples are scarce. Conversely, traditional Compressive Learning (IC) approaches rely on sample compression, which compromises dataset integrity and is unsuitable for regulatory compliance in sensitive fields. Our proposed solution, Compressive ICA, integrates both constraints to construct a robust representation from the full dataset using a minimal subset of data samples. It relies on non-convex optimization techniques to achieve a high-quality reconstruction of the ICA dictionary and data generation matrix. Our theoretical findings substantiate that Compressive ICA, employing specific帕雷托最优 solutions, guarantees a robust reconstruction of the ICA dictionary under specific conditions. Furthermore, we devise an efficient iterative solver based on alternating minimization and analyze its convergence properties. Our experiments demonstrate that Compressive ICA surpasses state-of-the-art icp methods in both accuracy and accuracy rate.

To analyze the interplay of species competition and dispersal, an asymmetric voter model incorporating diffusion noise was developed. This model incorporates three species, each possessing exclusive colonization areas, based on a competition-colonization trade-off. Depending on the diffusion noise level, the model exhibits two distinct regimes: 1) The regime of weak diffusion noise, where species coexistence is observed and driven by the balance of stochastic rates. 2) The regime of strong diffusion noise, characterized by species exclusion and governed by the competition-colonization trade-off without influence from detailed system settings. Consequently, the regime boundary serves as a dividing line, separating areas with varying probabilities of species persistence.
We prove that von Neumann algebras associated with compact regions within abelian quantum double models have infinite type $II$.

To enhance three-particle systems like magnons, photons, and phonons, researchers are exploring cavity magnomechanics as a novel platform for quantum information processing. They demonstrate entanglement among these components in a feedback loop involving an laser-driven magnomechanical circuit and an additional laser link between magnons and photons. This entanglement persists due to continuous measurement, exhibiting stronger correlations than magnon-photon interactions alone. They find that entanglement and the logarithmic negativity increase significantly with coherent feedback. However, certain conditions must be met for photon-pulses to remain entangled after spontaneous measurement according to Schrödinger's equation. They demonstrate entanglement among magnons, photons, and phonons in average and quantum states and show how coherent feedback affects the entanglement dynamics during phonon emission. They demonstrate that coherent feedback enhances entanglement between photons and phonons when phonons emit from the system.

We've obtained one-loop triple-collinear splitting operators for color and spin structures of dimension seven and eight, applicable to N$_{DR}$-$\overline{MS}$ gamma-matrix basis with dimensionality above six. Our results encompass all possible spin configurations and colors, with a specific focus on those of dimension six, which we previously derived and published. Calculations were conducted using the generalized unitary method and further refined through analytical techniques. We've verified our results by directly comparing them to the singular limits of tree-level products of six-, seven-, and eight-particle branch-cut integrals. These triple-collinear splitting operators play a crucial role in connecting lower and higher reduced phase-space singularities within QCD's factorization framework. Moreover, with adapted formulas, they facilitate the efficient evaluation of real-emission terms in next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order cross-section calculations for QCD processes.

A formal proof for the Neron Desingularization, a multidimensional case algorithm, has been formulated and applied to one-dimensional local rings, and this concept is currently being used within Singular software implementation. Furthermore, a relevant theorem based on Greenberg's Strong Approximation theorem has also been introduced and applied to the realm of one-dimensional local rings.

Ancient sundials served as primary timekeepers before the invention of mechanical clocks, with the classical Islamic civilization utilizing this method for both daily prayer schedules and almanacs. In contrast, the ancient Indonesians did not rely on sundials forprayer schedules due to the prevalence of Muslim communities in coastal areas with reliable sun exposure for calculating prayer times. However, historical and cultural sundials in Indonesia hold significant value beyond their practical value, reflecting both local knowledge of time measurement technology and foreign influence from the Islamic world. Despite their historical and cultural importance, these sundials have not been thoroughly researched due to limited scholarly attention and a lack of documentation. Recent digitization efforts have made studying ancient sundials in Indonesia more feasible, facilitating an examination of their unique features and characteristics through detailed analysis.

This research explores an integrated data and energy transmission network with D2D communications assisted by an IRS. To enhance the overall system data energy efficiency, we develop a joint optimization method for IRS parameters, D2D data transmission distance, and energy harvesting power. A three-part optimization method is then employed to solve a complex non-convex problem. Our method involves joint optimizing the IRS parameters and the power distribution among various nodes through discrete meta-heuristic algorithms. Subsequently, we use the WMMSE method to solve a non-convex subproblem related to the IRS parameters. Finally, we apply BMMSE to find the optimal D2D transmission distance. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving a superior overall system data energy efficiency.

The surge in telework needs has highlighted the potential benefits of fully
automating and controlling experiments remotely. This work presents the technical
advancements of developing a single-point LDV measurement acquisition system for
two-dimensional (2D) flows that can be operated and controlled entirely at a
distance. By utilizing a single-detector LDV system strategically positioned to
capture multiple measurement points, this research demonstrates the feasibility of
collecting planar measurements efficiently. Applied to the study of a 2D flow in
a circular cylinder behind a trailing vortex, the system's performance in remoting
the experiment setup was successfully showcased.

The cardinalities of finite models for theories with arbitrary relations of various arities are examined, particularly focusing on those containing binary relations. Despite recent breakthroughs in understanding this phenomenon for theories with only higher arity binary relations, a notable exception has been identified. It turns out that generalizing results from higher arity relations to binary relations yields incorrect conclusions.

The effectiveness of programmable electrostatic phase plates is subject of debate within the field. Recent data suggests that phase plates with minimal sizing can correct electron wave distortions more efficiently than traditional polymeric correctors. Our research investigates this phenomenon by employing a programmable electrostatic phase plate and a deformable membrane corrector to address wave distortions in the microscope's mid-plane. Our findings suggest that corrected electron waves exhibit comparable correcting capabilities to traditional polymers and, potentially, the coexistence of the phase plate and deformable membrane corrector could amplify their combined effectiveness.

Drawing inspiration from Feynman's and Deutsch's groundbreaking work, we introduce a theoretical framework that assesses computational capability across diverse physical platforms and complexity scales. This framework is utilized to analyze the fundamental principles of quantum computation. Furthermore, this study serves as a precursor to investigating more universal computation models by examining additional physical mechanisms exemplified throughout the paper.

This study focuses on determining the number of possible positions a random walker can occupy after $n$ steps in a $d$-dimensional lattice, denoted as $|S_n^{(d)}|$. We present a general formula in equation form, revealing that $|S_n^{(d)}|$ can be expressed as a sum involving binomial coefficients in multiple layers. We verify this finding using an inductive approach with combinatorial interpretations of the coefficients, distinguishing between even and odd values of $n$. In addition, we provide recursive relationships for both $S_n^{(d)}$ and $S_{n-1}^{(d)}$, enabling us to develop a straightforward calculation method for these set sizes. We demonstrate that this method encompasses well-known combinatorial sequences including central binomial coefficients, Catalan numbers, and their variants. Our findings also yield novel identities involving binomial coefficients, showcasing our main theorem's applicability.

This research in-depth examines the model of spherically symmetric polymer black holes, which was first introduced by Gambini, Olmedo, and Pullin within the framework of loop quantum gravity. We explored how in equipping this model with a specific frame, one can achieve coordinate extensions that eliminate singularities, both spatial and temporal, thus enabling us to calculate the geodesic motion of particles near these spherically symmetric polymer black holes. Furthermore, by establishing relationships between the parameters of polymer models and those of quantum gravity, we were able to compare our model with other polymer black holes and semi-classical torus solutions, both classically and through the calculation of their quasinormal frequency spectra. These computations not only demonstrate that our model can effectively regulate the Schwarzschild radius singularity, but also suggest that potential observations of quasinormal spectra from gravitational waves could provide evidence for loop quantum gravity effects at the Planck scale, rendering such effects accessible to scientists.

We have derived a semi-analytical formula for the dynamic density-density correlation of massless Dirac electrons in doped graphene, which is applicable at finite temperatures. This finding is key to understanding the thermal screening of interactions among Dirac electrons and has been used to calculate the specific heat and compressibility of undoped and doped graphene. In addition, the thermodynamic stability of undoped and doped graphene has been assessed. Moreover, the equation of state for doped graphene in the superlattice form (e.g., MoS2) has been established. Our research also highlights the need for a revised model of thermal phonons that accounts for the unique thermal properties of moiré superlattices in materials like twisted graphene.

Continuous speech leads to consistent prosodic patterns, contributing to the development of a monotonic pitch trajectory. Most speech synthesis systems employ a two-stage approach, beginning with coarse contour generation and refining it through the analysis-synthesis alignment of spectral features and prosodic patterns. MaskedSpeech, a novel prosody generation framework, directly generates a masked pitch contour by identifying and emphasizing masked regions within a speech frame. As a result, MaskedSpeech enhances synthetic prosody without the need for large-scale training data or recurrent neural networks. Experimental evaluations on three datasets demonstrate that MaskedSpeech significantly improves the quality of synthesized speech, demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing prosody.

We've enhanced projection predictive inference by enabling efficient selection of variables and structures in models beyond those in the exponential family. By projecting predictive variables into a latent space, we have created a generalized framework that: 1) maintains the original model's integrity while performing variable selection, 2) accurately detects relevant structures and retains posterior uncertainties, and 3) extends its applicability to non-Gaussian models within the exponential family. We've rigorously evaluated our approach by comparing it with established methods on various datasets, and the results demonstrate its superior performance in accurately selecting variables and recovering relevant structures.

Recent advances in large-scale machine learning have led to the development of state-of-the-art image classification models, primarily through deep neural networks trained on existing datasets. Our research investigates the potential vulnerabilities of these models when confronted with adversarial inputs generated by alternative generative models that have not been subjected to rigorous training. We demonstrate that even simplistic generative models can cause well-established classifiers to make unpredictable decisions, resulting in severe real-world consequences such as life-threatening errors in medical applications. Our findings reveal that existing defenses are ineffective in mitigating such threats, and that even top-performing generative models pose a significant risk. This underscores the critical need to evaluate generative models as adversarial inputs during training to prevent exploitable weaknesses.

Climate change communication is complicated by the proliferation of conspiracy theories, particularly those found online. This research investigates prevalent conspiracy theories regarding climate change by analyzing a significant Twitter dataset and applies a sophisticated stance detection technique. Our analysis focuses on whether such conspiracy theories are more widely shared by those who do not believe in climate change or those who do. Furthermore, we examine the most popular conspiracy theories, their variations with differing levels of climate change acceptance, and reveal that non-believers predominantly disseminate messages containing conspiracy theory-related keywords at nearly three times the rate of those who accept climate change.

A research study investigates the production of dark matter in proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV, either alongside a solitary top quark or in top quark pairs. The analysis utilizes data collected by the CMS experiment using a 36 million inverse picobarn dataset. Experiments are conducted across various final states characterized by isolated top quark or top quark pair jets and enhanced missing transverse momentum. Data obtained from these experiments align with predicted standards models within simulated experiments. Based on this information, confidence intervals are determined to quantify the cross-sectional differences between predicted and actual scenarios, which in turn enables the calculation of interaction limits. Furthermore, simplified models of top quark interactions with invisible partners are explored and related to the established standards models.

Given an n-exangulated category with specified properties, we establish that it satisfies Auslander-Reiten-Serre duality if and only if it possesses certain duality-based angles. We also determine a specific condition necessary for the presence of Serre duality. Assuming duality exists, we establish a one-to-one correspondence involving a bijection and specific category characteristics.

Building upon Kirkeboen et al.'s (2016) work that demonstrates the feasibility of combining multiple treatment instruments with ranked preference data, we analyze the testable implications of the key assumptions underpinning their identification argument. Our analysis reveals that these assumptions hold the following testable consequences: (i) the probit model's propensity scores accurately predict treatment rankings, and (ii) the choice of treatment within each ranking category is independent of unobserved factors influencing treatment preference, given observed covariates. Additionally, we present findings related to fields of study return estimates and confirm the empirical validity of these assumptions. Our results demonstrate a significant positive impact of increased fields of study returns on increased enrollment.

To advance our understanding of matter's diverse forms, high-energy particle collisions with a wide variety of projectiles must be conducted at super factories utilizing the J/psi resonance. Although previously explored extensively through electron-positron annihilation, utilizing J/psi resonance collisions offers distinct advantages, including accessing novel channels, producing abundant low-energy antiprotons ideal for high-precision experiments, and generating large quantities of rare particles like antineutrons and hyperons, facilitating new high-precision experiments. Moreover, future improvements in beam technology and detector capabilities promise even greater discoveries, driving new scientific inquiries.

Most of a multiple star system's final mass is expected to be acquired through discs that form during the process of disc accretion. Research has shown that these discs can trigger complex interactions between multiple stars, particularly those in triple systems, which often result in rapid changes to the system's configuration. Although it is widely accepted that these systems undergo unpredictable transformations during their early development, the factors that stabilize them are still unclear. To address this, scientists conducted detailed simulations of early triple systems that include the effects of the surrounding discs on the stars' interactions, which significantly impact the system's long-term behaviour. By taking into account the gradual accumulation of mass from the discs into the central stars, the researchers found that the central protostar can gradually gain control in a system that initially has equal-sized binary components, particularly as it grows in mass. As a result, such systems often develop into configurations where the central protostar is coupled with inner and outer companions that have disparate orbital scales. These results suggest that extensive accretion during early star formation may be triggered by interactions between the components of a system that is initially balanced in terms of stellar masses, which could potentially lead to the central protostar to acquire a considerable portion of its expected mass.

This study examines flat spacetimes with intrinsic simplicity, which become discrete when modeled after a lattice and retain their simplicity in the continuum limit. Researchers have historically regarded models with intrinsic simplicity as ideal representations for the matter content within General Relativity, but recent findings suggest that these few degrees of freedom might also incorporate gravitational effects seamlessly. Our research involves an in-depth analytical and numerical assessment of the model's feasibility in describing a standard four-parameter matter content - radiation, a cosmological constant, dark energy that decreases with time, and dust. We discover that the model can accurately reproduce specific solutions predicted by General Relativity under certain equation-of-state conditions but deviates from reality when the equation-of-state parameter falls within a certain range. We anticipate further research into this phenomenon and consider several potential avenues for exploration.

This paper presents a novel approach to solving the challenge of variational image segmentation, which is often plagued by issues such as noise and complex textures within various modalities. To address this, we devise a hybrid algorithm that integrates image segmentation, deconvolution, deblurring, and despeckling processes. By combining Perona-Malik flow models for both image segmentation and restoration in a single framework, our method efficiently handles degraded images in the spatial domain. Our approach demonstrates superior performance compared to existing methods in terms of speed and accuracy, particularly when dealing with images subjected to realistic degradations.

Active galactic nuclei (AGNs) comprising a central supermassive black hole and spinning matter accretion disk exhibit distinctive characteristics, including heavy iron emission at specific wavelengths, which can be linked to the black hole's mass and spin. Specifically, iron emission at 1.7 $\mu$m often displays features indicative of a rapidly spinning black hole. Researchers have proposed utilizing these features to constrain the mass and spin of the K2186 black hole, a quasars with iron at 1.7 $\mu$m suggesting a rapidly spinning black hole. If such a black hole interacts with an ultralight scalar or pseudoscalar field, rapid spin through superradiance may instability enhance its mass within a specified range. If K2186's mass and spin are subject to these constraints, it implies a specific non-zero mixing of the electron neutrino with these bosons at a level of approximately 0.07 eV. If this occurs, it could also affect other aspects of neutrino physics, including its oscillation parameters and potential implications for other phenomena.

Creating intelligent, neuroinspired systems poses a significant challenge due to intricate design and implementation hurdles, including a significant discrepancy between modeling fidelity and research timelines. Utilizing existing hardware platforms with different design architectures, including logic-based and spiking neural network (SNN) based systems, is a practical solution to this problem. In this study, we developed an emulator named BrianLoihi that combines Brian's neural network simulator with Intel's multi-core Loihi chip. By embedding Brian in a software development kit (SDK), we enabled seamless development of intelligent applications on the Loihi platform. Our demonstration involved replicating a spiking working memory model on both software (Brian) and hardware (Loihi) platforms, comparing the performance of a 512-neuron loop and a 5120-neuron cloud model. Our research showcases a timeline acceleration of at least two orders of magnitude, including a 2000-fold increase for the cloud model, on the Loihi platform compared to traditional workstations.

A solar type-I noise storm is known to be generated by turbulent plasma occurring near stronger localized areas of stronger magnetic fields and is characterized by significant amplitude variations on a microsecond scale. Understanding the dynamics of flaring plasma requires detailed analysis of storm parameters and their relationship with complex magnetic field configurations. This study investigates the dynamics of a coronal plasma through the detailed analysis of a type-I burst and sub-bursts generated during a minor flare on November 15, 2013. The research involves in-depth computer simulations of magnetic field configurations at the emission sources of the storm. The results reveal that the type-I burst originates from stronger magnetic field regions and exhibits higher amplitude variations, while the type-I sub-bursts originate from weaker magnetic field areas. The findings also indicate that minor flare activities can lead to the generation of both strong and weak magnetic field regions. The research also reveals a correlation between temporal and spatial evolution of storm features. These results have significant implications for further research in this field.

A compact magneto-optical trap has been successfully developed, using a planar-integrated design that merges an optical grating chip and a magnetic coil chip. This novel setup minimizes the size and weight of the trap, requiring only a single laser beam to capture a population of approximately 10,000 cold rubidium atoms. The improved MOT architecture has potential applications in devices demanding reduced dimensions, such as hybrid micro-electro-mechanical systems, quantum sensors, and nuclear fusion reactors with inertial confinement.

The spherically symmetric merging process of a kinetic cloud of particles onto a Schwarzschild black hole is investigated. Unlike earlier studies, which relied on a point of infall, our work incorporates finite-sized surfaces on both poles and the equator of the sphere. As a result, the assumption of spherical symmetry is disrupted before the particles reach the event horizon, leading to non-zero angular momentum around the black hole. This results in an uneven distribution of matter, with the side facing the black hole experiencing fewer particles merging than the opposite side. Our findings reveal that the angular momentum effect can be substantial, particularly at larger radii, with the exchange between this momentum and the radial infall velocity causing a significant decrease in merging rate.

The probability of (de-)excitation and photon emission is evaluated for a non-relativistic, moving atom interacting with a quantum electromagnetic field near a stationary, perfectly conducting plane. These findings expand upon previous scalar model outcomes where the atom was represented by a scalar variable coupled to a scalar field with either Dirichlet or Neumann conditions applied on the boundary. This study considers a dipole moment fixed in direction and examines how long-term emission rates fluctuate periodically. For motion speeds much lower than the light speed, significant findings include increased emission probabilities during excitation compared to decay when the atom moves towards the mirror, accompanied by the appearance of emitted energy spectra at impossible frequencies for stationary atoms. In contrast, these models predict reduced emission rates during both excitation and decay when the atom moves away from the mirror. Energy transfer to the field generally occurs when the atom moves in a specific polarization-dependent way below a specific frequency threshold ($\gamma$) applied globally across all transition frequencies. However, above this threshold, the atoms tend to gain energy through enhanced photon emission.

A 10 million solar mass young cluster called Westerlund 2 lies at the center of a vast and unusual star-forming region within the 30 degree Tarantula Nebula, nestled in the Large Magellanic Cloud. This unprecedented region is characterized by numerous dense and open clusters scattered throughout, including several members shrouded in gas-forming nebulosity. Our analysis, utilizing spectroscopic observations from the MUSE instrument, reveals numerous massive stars within Westerlund 2's surroundings that exhibit striking chemical peculiarities, including rich helium abundance signatures indicative of massive B-type stars and massive populations containing early B-type members. These discoveries imply the presence of massive star formation occurring outside of Westerlund 2, which is the dense and unusual cluster at study's core. Our data also indicate the existence of numerous lower-mass stars within Westerlund 2's hinterlands that are yet to be discovered. These discoveries provide valuable insights into the complex and unusual process of massive star formation occurring within this core cluster at study's core, which is the dense and unusual cluster at study's core, which is the dense and unusual cluster at study's core.

Degraded handwritten documents, which are often affected by factors such as poor paper quality, degraded ink, and awkward writing postures, can pose significant transcription challenges. Consequently, an advanced document image enhancement technique is essential for successful handwritten text recognition and reading. In this study, we introduce Multi-HBE, a novel end-to-end handwritten document image enhancement framework that simultaneously improves degraded images and generates images resembling original manuscripts through a dual-task approach. By integrating a proposed adversarial network with prior work, Multi-HBE successfully produces improved images and original-like images. Moreover, the effectiveness of this framework has been demonstrated through superior performance in handwritten text recognition experiments, particularly on the Archaic Italian Document Handwriting Recognition (AIDHR) dataset. Notably, the proposed Multi-HBE framework achieves remarkable results on the AIDHR dataset, delivering both high overall accuracy of 77.01% and a character-level accuracy of 74.36%. Furthermore, the proposed framework has demonstrated exceptional effectiveness on the AIDHR dataset in handwritten OCR tasks, outperforming state-of-the-art models.

The use of OCR technology often necessitates manual correction due to its limitations, which can be mitigated by utilizing NLP techniques. Despite the availability of specialized tools for processing ID cards, they tend to be expensive and require substantial manual intervention. This research demonstrates the efficacy of using standard OCR and NLP components, specifically Keras-Tesseract for OCR and Spacy for NLP, to facilitate the extraction of information from Indonesian ID cards. The results show that this approach significantly enhances data accuracy and allows for automatic correction of misinterpreted data, with information reorganized in a structured manner. Compared to existing ID extraction software, this method offers a more cost-effective solution, with the added benefit of requiring minimal manual correction.

In vehicular communication systems operating under the IEEE 802.11p standard, channel estimation is crucial for optimizing performance. To achieve optimal channel estimation, extensive pilots are required; however, they consume valuable spectrum resources, which needs to be carefully balanced. As a solution, a novel IEEE 802.11p-compliant channel estimation approach based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, enhanced with temporal averaging, is proposed in this study.
