By leveraging the memory capabilities of LSTM, the framework minimizes the number of required pilots, leading to improved spectrum efficiency. Extensive simulations demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed scheme, channelizing the IEEE 802.11p standard and operating across different vehicle distances, thereby validating its applicability in real-world scenarios.

The task of automatically assigning colors to images without human input proves challenging due to limited color information in grayscale images, resulting in color ambiguities. Recent advancements have involved leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) in conjunction with color ambiguity loss functions to address color ambiguity and automate colorization, although these models often suffer from unstable training issues stemming from color ambiguity's non-differentiability. We propose a novel approach that overcomes these limitations by using a series of well-trained trained GANs trained on diverse astronomical images, which are then composed into a multi-stage image processing pipeline. This model not only enhances colorization accuracy but also improves visual quality and achieves image upscaling capabilities, effectively outperforming previous methods on various datasets, which are publicly available for further research and development.

We've developed a novel approach to train feedforward neural networks that don't rely on differentiability, particularly for cases where traditional back-propagation fails. By providing a new proof of the Universal Approximation Theorem, we've established that any continuous function can be accurately represented by a neural network with fewer layers. Our innovative algorithm mimics back-propagation's results but doesn't require differentiability, enabling its application to both smooth and non-smooth optimization problems. Our experiments demonstrate significant improvements over current training methods, particularly for cases where back-propagation is infeasible.

The ECFA Early Career Researcher's panel started representing the interests of young researchers within the ECFA community in January 2021. Throughout its first two years of operation, the panel developed its organizational framework, cooperated with ECFA by offering input and insights, and introduced several projects focused on comprehending and addressing the varied needs of young researchers. This report outlines the details of the panel's formation and operations as well as its engagement with numerous activities during its first two years of operation.

Confining modes at the intersection of two interfaces has garnered significant interest due to its extensive applications in optical communications and laser technology. However, in recent years, research has focused on coupling between light strands rather than on the fundamental interaction of particles of light. We have developed a method to describe the behavior of line waves at a boundary of two optical surfaces, which can control both lateral and vertical movement line waves effectively. Our theoretical framework and simulations demonstrate control over the lateral and vertical dispersion of line waves at the interface between a pair of metasurfaces line supports, which can be tuned by adjusting the parameters of metasurfaces line. We propose a practical line support configuration that supports a variety of line wave patterns, such as line waves moving in opposite directions, line waves moving vertically, and stationary line waves. Our approach offers a new perspective on light manipulation and provides a framework line support configuration that can be used in optical technology and line-wave-based line switching systems.

One of the most significant challenges to deploying commercially viable commercial robots lies in overcoming individual differences in learning capabilities between humans and robots. To create robots that can effectively learn to collaborate with humans, it is essential to develop new cognitive architectures that enable human-like learning. Building robust computational models of human decision-making processes is another critical step towards achieving this goal. Such models can aid in identifying collaborative strategies that maximize collaboration outcomes. Our research focuses on developing an open and adaptable cognitive architecture for multi-agent collaborative learning through the integration of advanced machine learning and decision analysis techniques. This architecture can model complex human-robot interactions by combining multiple learning methods to model and predict behaviors of both human and robotic agents. By utilizing scenarios that simulate real-world collaborative tasks, our cognitive architecture promotes the development of robot behaviors that are adaptable to human variations, thereby enhancing their ability to cooperate effectively.

A new bias-corrected estimator has been created for the mean absolute deviation of a median regression model, addressing the problem of irregularity that typically challenges bias reduction in derivative-type estimates.  To overcome this issue, a novel approach involving local linear modeling of the absolute deviation function is employed.  Under certain conditions, it is demonstrated that the proposed method can consistently and efficiently estimate the desired quantity, specifically when the explanatory variables follow a normal distribution, it is shown that the method remains asymptotically unbiased.  The development of suitable confidence intervals is also explored, highlighting the importance of choosing appropriate intervals to maintain correct coverage probabilities in low-sample scenarios.

The tasks of relation extraction and knowledge graph link prediction share a
common ground in predicting a subject's relations and objects, making them closely
related. Specifically, successful MR can supply knowledge graph link prediction
with accurate entity alignments, and conversely, PKGLP can supply MR with reliable
entity embeddings, thereby enhancing relational features and boosting overall
performance on the MR task. In this study, we investigate the dual utilization of
each task to improve one another, employing the proposed models on a publicly
available dataset and demonstrating improved results compared to current methods.

The Analytical Exact Iteration Method is employed to solve quarkonium dissociation states in an $N$-dimensional space with an anisotropic momentum. By considering finite-temperature and finite-baryonic-chemical-potential conditions within an anisotropic frame, we derive the thermally-modified quasi-particle Debye mass in an anisotropic frame. Using finite-baryonic-chemical-potential and intrinsic mass, we solve quarkonium bound mass spectra in an anisotropic frame. We investigate the dissociation potential and mass spectra of quarkonium bound states in both anisotropic and isotropic media. Our analysis reveals that media anisotropy and finite-baryonic-chemical-potential significantly impact quarkonium dissociation. In comparison to anisotropic and finite-baryonic-chemical-potential, the combined perturbative Wakamatsu potential in an anisotropic media exhibits a weaker dissociation and higher bound mass spectra.

Our study focused on the magnetic arrangement within the crystals of Tb3RuO7 and Nd3RuO7 using neutron diffraction. We found that Tb3RuO7 exhibits magnetic ordering with a periodicity of 4 x 10 x 12 Angstrom at 17.6 Angstrom and exhibits temperature-dependent behavior transitioning from a disordered to a new state in the 17.6 to 15.6 Angstrom range. Neither Tb3RuO7 nor Nd3RuO7 exhibited spiral magnetic structure as observed in related compounds. Instead, both compounds displayed magnetic arrangements characterized by spin rotations within the plane perpendicular to the atomic plane. In Nd3RuO7, one lattice vector shows a specific order at both neutron and synchrotron resonant x-ray diffraction, indicating a tiny tilt of the spin from the plane perpendicular to the plane. In Tb3RuO7, a partially disordered state appears under a non-uniform internal magnetic field, leading to resonance differences in neutron and synchrotron diffraction.

Many complex systems, such as those through which light passes, can be characterized by their linear transformation properties, efficiently described using complex matrices known as Dirac operators, especially when periodicity is involved. Despite the widespread use of Dirac operators in theoretical physics, their application has been relatively limited in the analysis of general periodic systems, particularly in scenarios involving multiple modulation frequencies. Our proposed solution is the Modulated Periodic Activations network, an advanced neural architecture designed to extract local characteristics from one-dimensional periodic systems, effectively utilizing the principles of quantum mechanics. This innovative method enables high-precision determination of key characteristics, including the topological charge and effective potential of a system, even parameters that are otherwise obscure. Its versatility is evident in its successful implementation across diverse quantum phenomena, including the Haldane model, Thouless pumping and generalization to systems with multi-frequency modulations.

We introduce a novel semi-supervised approach that integrates traditional classification techniques with generative methods to adapt to changes in data distribution. This approach leverages semi-supervised info-maximization techniques to learn causal features, enabling effective adaptation to distributional shifts. By focusing on underrepresented classes within hidden causal components, this method achieves accurate classifications even in the presence of label noise. Moreover, this new technique combines the benefits of supervised learning of causal features and unsupervised distributional shift adaptation methods, all while requiring only a causal understanding of the underlying data. Thorough experiments conducted on synthetic, benchmark, and real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of this method over contemporary state-of-the-art techniques.

Despite its impressive task execution capabilities, the inner workings of deep learning systems remain shrouded in theoretical uncertainty. In our study, we establish a geometric model for deep learning architectures by identifying connections to pre-existing geometric frameworks in quantum computation and diffeomorphic template matching. Within this context, we map the geometric structures of convolutional neural networks, residual networks, recursive neural networks, recurrent neural networks, and the equilibrium propagation framework. Furthermore, this geometric framework enables us to explore the relationships between geometric structures and the performance of different neural networks, thereby guiding the design of deep learning architectures at an algorithmic level.

We examine the outcomes of Kenkichi Iwasawa's principal factors theorem, emphasizing its connection to the geometric approach of Lattice Theory. Our investigation focuses on the relationship between minimal elements in certain subsets of Iwasawa's tree and the structure of solvable algebraic groups, particularly for groups with two non-trivial factors, where we demonstrate that these minima correspond to extreme lattice minima. Additionally, we provide a lattice-based proof of the principal factors theorem and speculatively offer a method for generalizing it.

A research framework is introduced to uncover and analyze decision-making processes of pre-trained machine learning models without altering their predictions, specifically through the use of layer-wise relevance propagation in the context of jet classification. By examining variables pre-selected by experimental physicists, we are able to map neural network layers to these variables and identify variable-layer relationships within pre-trained models without post-training analysis. On the other hand, tethered explanations are used to showcase how specific input variables influence intermediate network outputs. Results from simulations based on proton proton collisions predict that pre-trained models prioritize novel variables over traditional ones, while highlighting the critical role of intermediate network nodes.

For every positive integer r with an associated Stirling number, we define a generalized version with respect to a degenerate variable. This generalized version breaks down into four different forms based on numbers representing permutations with a specific number of cycles. We examine the properties of these forms and provide an identity in the number degenerate-Nosonberler polynomial space.

Eighty sets of layer groups were examined, each consisting of four types: ordinary and double, as well as gray single and double. Layer group properties allowed for the efficient computation of relevant physical characteristics using symbolic methods, thanks to code such as POLSym. This involved an initial step of categorizing irreducible domains based on their action within the Brillouin zone and the topology of the torus. Additionally, small cofactor groups were found, which influenced the irreducible representation sets through site symmetry reduction. These sets were then subjected to site symmetry reduction, resulting in as many as eight sets for each layer group configuration. This resulted in a total of 64 set combinations, for which irreducible representation sets were computed. These results provided foundational knowledge on lattice dynamics for nano and micro structures, as well as other applications requiring band structure knowledge. The findings are publicly available on the web.

Momentum operators are explored in the context of Dirac fields, specifically focusing on those defined by Killing vector fields with geodesic integral curves. The study derives expressions for Killing vector components and demonstrates that curvature components must satisfy specific conditions for the operator to be valid. Classified by symmetry groups, solutions to curvature constraints are identified for spaces with various isometry groups, and corresponding momentum operator expressions are provided. Classified by symmetry groups, solutions to curvature constraints are identified for spaces with various isometry groups, and corresponding momentum operator expressions are provided.

A sign problem encountered in Monte Carlo simulations beyond half-filling can be mitigated by transforming the integration path. However, this transformation introduces additional complexities in terms of noise. Our proposed architecture integrates a network of neurons with complex values and employs it to develop a wave function parameterization based on spin rotations. This new approach enables accurate representations of many-body wave functions without incurring extra noise. As a tangible illustration, we precisely model the Hubbard model's ground state across various spin configurations using our method.

In this research, we explore composite flavon-Higgs models where the Standard Model is integrated with global symmetries, which contain both flavon and fermion components, as non-linear sigma model targets. The model's features allow us to investigate its non-perturbative aspects within a large N framework. The analysis reveals that a unique vev configuration for the flavons emerges from non-perturbative dynamics, yielding non-zero masses for the light fermions. Furthermore, we investigate the possibility of preserving global symmetries and determine their relationship with the flavon potential. The analysis of the flavon potential also indicates that the Nc/32 value is a stable fixed point under certain conditions. The study of the root superpotential and its original interpretation as an axion in the 4D case provides insights into the supergravitational origin of the model. Finally, the possibility of spontaneous breaking of global symmetries leads to the appearance of Goldstone bosons along with the Higgs and technicolor sectors from the non-perturbative dynamics.

The use of Virtual-Physical Perceptual Manipulations, like redirected walking and haptics, extends VR interaction beyond conventional physical limitations by exploiting the boundaries of human perception, subtly guiding users' movements to enhance interactivity. This research examines the dangers of VPPM exploitation, beginning with a conceptual framework that confirms their existence and then applying speculative design to identify and mitigate threats. Through practical examples, we demonstrate how current VPPM practices can inadvertently create vulnerabilities that may lead to physical harm. This study seeks to highlight the potential consequences of VPPM applications and dissemination as they stand today.

To assess various approaches to expanding language coverage, we integrate German and Korean into BigScience's large-scale, 1.3 billion parameter multilingual language model, initially trained on 13 languages. Our study focuses on key factors influencing model adaptability for new languages and weighs the computational expense against potential performance gains.

Recent breakthroughs in numerical simulations of binary system formation through core fragmentation have enabled researchers to investigate the topic in great detail. Through various simulations, scholars have examined the total mass of primordial binaries under diverse initial conditions, uncovering the influence of core mass and angular momentum on final system mass. Our investigation aims to bridge a critical gap in current understanding by exploring the formation mass of binaries resulting from the collapse of cores initially comprising 0.3 solar masses, but gradually accreting up to 1.5 solar masses. Utilizing adaptive mesh refinement and a high-resolution logarithmic radial grid, and employing a grid with over 100 million cells, we were able to resolve the collapse and disruption of cores spanning 0.01 to 0.1 parsecs in diameter across 0.01 to 0.3 solar masses. Our data reveal that as core mass increases, the mass of resulting binaries also increases. Furthermore, our findings indicate that a significant fraction of a core's mass concentrates within 0.01 parsecs and ultimately forms within 0.001 parsecs. An empirical formula representing the relationship between binary system mass and parent core mass has been developed based on our and previous studies, demonstrating that the mass ratio of binaries to clusters follows a power law with a slope of -1.5.

This research introduces m-arcsin-transformed Gaussian components into a new model for non-Gaussian data analysis known as the m-Fast model. We rationally derive these components by applying a power-transformed likelihood method and demonstrate their relationship with the super-Gaussian data model. We develop a novel optimization method called Fast Fixed-Point, which achieves efficient maximum likelihood estimation for the model. Furthermore, we enhance its performance by implementing a novel procedure to determine the arc-sin-transformed scale parameters. Our method, m-ar-K-Fast, exhibits superior convergence and reconstruction quality compared to existing methods, even in the absence of higher-order moments. Our findings are supported by our theoretical analysis, which also provides a novel probabilistic interpretation of the sign-transformed estimation method. Additionally, we numerically verify the theoretical results and show that m-ar-K-Fast surpasses existing methods in terms of convergence, robustness, and reconstruction quality.

This paper builds on existing research linking finite model theory to algebraic and propositional proof systems. It's proven that if a logic system can differentiate between all pairs of graphs in a specific category, then its associated proof system polynomial-time encompasses a wide range of graph types. This result is achieved by refining an earlier approach, yielding more rapid runtimes by an exponential factor compared to previous findings. Furthermore, the study provides concrete examples illustrating how certain polynomial-calculus axials can simulate first-order logic properties, while others can do the same for fixed-point polynomial calculus. Notably, the revised example requires significantly lower runtime compared to prior studies.

A subring collection is deemed $\sigma$- elementary if it exhibits closure under operations of direct sums, maps and embeddings. In 2008, M. Morfina established a connection to the $\sigma$-hereditary order on the lattice of ring isomorphism classes, which led to the identification of numerous subcollection families of rings with $\sigma$- elementary properties and distinct order positions. Building of his work, the authors not only extend and refine Morfina's results but also establish a relationship between $\sigma$- elementary rings and their prime versions, identifying an infinite prime ring family mapping to $\sigma$- idealizable Artinian ring family, which are $\sigma$- elementary and $\sigma$- invariant under isomorphism. Additionally, the theorems provided allow for the simplification of the proof of Morfina's main result and offer a demonstration of the partial order equality among a specific subcollection family, previously established by Morfina.

Many assertions made in public discourse cannot be disproven due to a lack of clear evidence against them. For instance, certain political leaders may claim responsibility for unfavorable economic conditions, citing control over fiscal and monetary policies. However, disproving such assertions would require evidence of another set of circumstances. A notable example is the claim made by a White House official in 2009 that he could not be held responsible for the economic downturn because circumstances beyond his control were at fault. Classifying and understanding the structure of such claims in contemporary politics is challenging, particularly given their inherent inability to be disproven. This study contributes to the ongoing debate on truth in public discourse by offering a systematic approach to identify and categorize such claims through natural language processing. Our methodology involves annotating data and employing machine learning to detect these assertions in news headlines and articles about major political figures since 2009. The resulting dataset reveals an increase in the frequency of such claims made by prominent politicians in the US, the UK, and Germany. Subsequent qualitative analyses of these claims highlight their distinct features and implications. Ultimately, this research proposes a framework that facilitates the comparison and evaluation of such claims based on key attributes and implications.

Identifying trending social media events in real-time across various geographical locations is crucial, particularly for anticipating potential disruptions such as transportation incidents, unusual weather conditions, and significant protests. The dynamic nature of social media data poses a challenge, given its rapid content creation rate and constantly evolving patterns of language use. Our solution utilizes a specialized machine learning model that recognizes temporal patterns in social media texts to detect emerging events. By incorporating spatial filters based on location tags, we pinpoint situations occurring within specific areas, effectively filtering out ubiquitous events like rolling news. Our approach was evaluated against actual social media data sets and showed promising results.

New, high-precision data from the cosmic microwave background lensing and tomographic galaxy surveys will facilitate the study of galaxy non-linear evolution through novel statistical tools, such as the bispectrum. However, existing techniques for analyzing the baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) power spectrum are limited. A major challenge lies in efficiently processing large datasets, which current methods struggle to do without significantly hampering computational feasibility. In response, a new fast simulation method has been proposed. By sampling the 2D Fourier space using a tilted grid, this approach accelerates simulations while retaining fidelity with a traditional grid. enhancements, such as compensating weights, further improve accuracy by accounting for uneven sampling. Results demonstrate that this approach can rapidly evaluate large-scale galaxy surveys, such as the 2degField example. Rapidly calculating the BAO contribution in the legged bispectrum configuration allows researchers to accurately extract non-BAO signal and efficiently perform residual analysis. These results suggest the approach is suitable for realistic surveys predicted in the near future, offering a valuable tool for future CMB lensing and large-scale structure studies.

We establish a statistical framework for classifying and regressing under adversarial conditions, leveraging Bayesian inference. By drawing from a pre-trained model and accounting for potential adversarial perturbations, our method generates a sample from the posterior distribution, thus accounting for uncertainty. Expanding upon previous work on certifiable predictions, our approach produces predictions with higher accuracy and greater certainty. Empirical results from synthetic and natural image datasets confirm the benefits of our method in terms of accuracy and robustness.

The COVID-19 pandemic spread globally in early 2020, with China experiencing extreme cases in January and February. This period fueled the explosion of online rumors regarding the pandemic, presenting a severe threat to public health safety and social stability. Understanding and predicting the dissemination pattern and magnitude of rumors is essential. This research aimed to discover the mechanism behind the rapid dissemination of online rumors and assess their dissemination speed and range using a Logisitic growth model. To this end, we analyzed the temporal pattern of rumor propagation from January to February 2020 on Sina Weibo, simulating the logistic growth model using Lasso regression. This model was found to provide an outstanding fit to the data, with notable predictions of the ultimate dissemination speed and range of five prominent pandemic-related rumors.

This research investigates the impact of hyperspectral pixel dimensionality reduction on classification tasks. Various methods are employed to reduce dimensions from 302 down to 3, utilizing techniques such as principal component analysis, and evaluating their effectiveness using the Darrisaw benchmark dataset and the Darrisaw evaluator. Experimental results reveal that certain dim reduction approaches enhance classification accuracy, yet some methods significantly decrease accuracy. Interestingly, some techniques that degrade performance improve human visual interpretation of the spectra, suggesting a potential connection between spectral dim reduction methods that improve human understanding and dimensionality reduction methods that also reduce dimensions for improved classification results.

Neural networks are highly effective at solving complex tasks, but they often require significant computational resources to operate. The large size of modern networks makes training and inference processes resource-intensive. The issue of model compression has garnered substantial interest due to its potential to reduce the size of models, making them faster to train and query. While model compression techniques have been extensively explored for KNN models, language model compression remains under-researched. Our work introduces a comprehensive survey of the latest advancements in KNN language model compression, providing a detailed examination of various methods and highlighting future research avenues.

A novel prediction method, referred to as ProCS, generates high-quality estimates for amide proton chemical shifts in proteins using sophisticated quantum mechanics calculations in relatively short times - about 30 million operations per residue, making it feasible to evaluate a 70-residue chain in under two days. ProCS predictions were compared with both theoretical and experimental data, complementing existing structure validation techniques by efficiently analyzing protein and side-chain hydrogen bonds. These predictions enabled accurate modeling of challenging protein structures through energy minimization and refinement using restraints based on ProCS ProCS predictions were applied in two challenging cases - validating the structure of ubiquitin and refining a fuzzy intrinsically disordered protein segment in histone deacetylase 3. Our research reveals the potential for ProCS to rapidly and reliably validate mid-sized proteins and refine disordered protein structures through high-quality predictions of amide proton chemical shifts in a computationally efficient timeframe.

The choice of loss function for a neural network is crucial as it guides the training process. Despite being widely used, research on how different loss functions affect classification performance in multiclass scenarios is limited. This study examines the influence of commonly used classifiers, including Cross-Entropy, Hinge, and Huber losses, on classification performance in such tasks. Through experimental research, it reveals that while Cross-Entropy loss often achieves the highest accuracy, particularly with one-hot loss encoding, other setups can lead to unexpected results. Notably, using the Label Encoding method and combining it with Huber loss obtained a surprisingly better score of 0.866 AUC-ROC area, exceeding the cross-entropy score of 0.808. These findings suggest that the performance gap can be significantly reduced, and this research aims to identify the underlying reasons and develop more effective strategies to address the issue of varying results across different loss functions and evaluation metrics in neural network classification.

Conformally representing the four-point function in a diamond shape facilitates a symmetric and comprehensive interpretation of the parquet equations used to describe interactions in systems with strong dependencies. However, solving the nonlinear parquet equations in this representation involves eliminating discontinuities, which is typically achieved through sorting and thresholding, thus compromising the analytic and microscopic understanding of the solutions. To overcome this limitation, we propose a new framework, the t-chain mapping, within the conformal representation to circumvent discontinuities. By rewriting the parquet equations in terms of various t-channel responses involving intermediate propagators and vertices, we successfully avoid discontinuities and ensure their cancellation without imposing additional constraints. Furthermore, we highlight the connection between these t-chain responses and the embedded Hamiltonian problem, specifically relating to the correlation functions of these systems.

The process of exciton condensation leading to a quantum phase transition in an otherwise normal state is the subject of extensive theoretical research. To study this phenomenon in detail to two dimensions, theoretical models are developed. Although previous studies provided valuable insights into critical behavior and support experimental findings, they relied on simplified assumptions. To improve these models, researchers employed the random phase approximation in self-consistent calculations, taking into account the interactions between excitons and charged carriers properly in both spatial momentum components. To validate the theoretical models and their results, studies were conducted on $\bf TiSe_2$, a material known to undergo exciton condensation. To further refine the models' accuracy, interactions between excitons and charged carriers were measured precisely. To thoroughly investigate the effects of these interactions, various properties of $\bf TiSe_2$ were studied, including its electronic structure, spectral function, and response functions to light and electronic probes. To better understand the impact of these interactions, researchers also measured the material's key physical properties. To better match experimental findings, researchers considered the effects of disorder on the material's electronic structure. To better understand the material's behavior, studies were conducted at different temperatures. To better match experimental findings, researchers also measured the material's thermodynamic properties. To further validate the theoretical models, researchers compared their results with the material's experimental data. To better understand the material's behavior, researchers also measured the material's thermodynamic properties.

In the US, dispatchers play a crucial role in coordinating community safety by processing thousands of calls annually, directing emergency services and gathering critical safety information from callers. Traditionally, this vital knowledge has been captured during calls via structured notes, such as crime types and suspect descriptions, through a collaborative process with law enforcement agencies and the media. Our study delves into the unnoticed dynamics of dispatcher-community interactions by analyzing a large dataset of text-based call reports in San Francisco from 2013 to 2018. By combining NLP techniques with statistical event sequence analysis, we successfully identify essential call details and track their progression over time, showcasing notable long-term trends in community safety data.

To analyze the impact of external magnetic fields on spin-triplet n-superconductors with nematic properties, we employed the local density approximation to calculate their absolute magnetization. Our results demonstrate that the susceptibility of such triplet superconductors can be enhanced by magnetic fields aligned with their transport direction and that this increase in susceptibility can serve as a clear indicator of triplet pairing through specific measurements, such as muon spin rotation experiments. Furthermore, our calculations reveal distinct patterns of density modifications within these superconductors when subjected to magnetic fields oriented both parallel and perpendicular to their transport direction, exhibiting opposite responses in certain regions. Our theoretical predictions are consistent with experimental observations in NixV_4S_8 and can also be applied to analyze similar materials like MoGe nanowires that exhibit unconventional triplet pairing characteristics.

Label-efficient active learning strategies are crucial for managing data annotation expenses. Presently, many practical approaches focus on minimizing prediction uncertainty to select informative samples for annotation. However, from a game-theoretic perspective, uncapped uncertainty minimization can lead to suboptimal results against certain data selection sequences. A worst-case analysis of the uncertainty-minimization method reveals its limitations, prompting the development of a new uncertainty measure that incorporates both risk and variation, and is used to create a minimax active learning algorithm. This measure, referred to as the absolute deviation risk, is proven to yield a more stable selection process, and is shown through theoretical and empirical evidence to outperform established methods in diverse settings, particularly when the label space is extensively defined.

To study changes in Western art music from 1950 to 2020, we employed measures of entropy and entropy rate from information theory as the song and artist entropies, respectively. By analyzing thousands of songs per decade, we revealed specific patterns in the entropy of individual artists and the overall entropy of each decade, which show non-trivial evolutionary trends. We found that artists initially display random-like behavior with high entropy, but over time develop a unique style, resulting in lower entropy. When comparing multiple artists, those with similar styles display dependencies between their music, resulting in negative shifts in entropy. However, when artists explore new genres, their music becomes more random-like, resulting in increased entropy. These results can aid music curators in understanding music similarities and dependencies, ultimately aiding the creation of effective playlists that balance repetition and novelty.

A novel category of stochastic processes that incorporate reinforcement involves sequences of random process entries derived from multiple independent draws, each with a corresponding weight, splitting operator, or both applied to them. Our study, which generalizes previously studied models such as the Pólya urn and branching processes with non-negative immigration, proves that certain conditions on the model parameters lead to specific properties, including finite moments and asymptotic distributions for entry size, particularly notable is our finding that process entries converge exponentially to 0 or 0 normally distributed, which holds under broad parameters for branching processes with non-negative immigration. Additionally, our results reveal that conditions that lead to finite moments are slightly more restrictive than conditions that lead to exponential convergence. Finally, we utilize our findings to establish a strong law of large numbers and a central limit theorem for sum over an arbitrary number of steps of the weights assigned to entries within this process.

Prawitz identified key characteristics of constructive proof within his concept of a constructive universal, which formed the basis of early proof theory. By incorporating Girard's novel interpretations of cuts and cut-elimination, derived from linear logic, I aim to re-examine and ultimately explain the foundation of proof theory. By introducing the ideas of formulas as processes, display proofs, and the show, I not only provide a new perspective on proof but also simplify and clarify established results within the naturalistic approach to proof theory.

A prominent paradigm in reward learning utilizes human feedback via comparative evaluations, but their widespread adoption is hindered by the expense and labor intensity of these comparisons. To overcome this limitation, we propose grouping multiple comparisons together and allowing human labelers to mark sub-regions of a condensed state space representation, thereby efficiently utilizing human time. Through data visualization techniques, we create an interactive interface for users to label these regions, thereby effectively enhancing the learning agents' performance, even when human labeling time remains constant, across basic Mujoco tasks.

We show that a topological space's Smyth powerspace is core-compact if and only if the original space has local compactness. Consequently, this implies the Smyth powerspace does not uniformly preserve core-compact properties.

We're investigating singular vorticities in ideal two-dimensional fluids with specific properties derived from point vortices and vortex sheets. These characteristics are embodied in "pointed vortex loops," allowing us to concentrate on their corresponding orbits under area-preserving diffeomorphisms on the 2D real plane. The results show that a specific subgroup within these diffeomorphisms preserves the shape of the vortex loop itself, indicating the configuration space is comprised of loops confining a fixed area regardless of the vorticity distribution and any connected points.

The Average Treatment Effect (ATE) is a crucial concept in causal inference that aids researchers and policymakers in understanding the nuanced impacts of various observables on treatment and outcome variables.  In circumstances where treatment variables are intricately linked with observables and unobservables, obtaining an unbiased estimate of ATE through outcome modeling alone may prove misleading due to model misspecification.  To address this issue, recent studies have developed machine learning-based outcome modeling procedures paired with outcome modeling orthogonality conditions.  Although these approaches yield consistent ATE estimates under outcome modeling misspecification, they can experience significant efficiency losses.  A new method is introduced here that incorporates probability inversion weighting (PIW) into the machine learning procedure to mitigate this efficiency loss.  Unlike traditional PIW, which utilizes outcome modeling predictions alone, our proposed method utilizes information from both the treatment variable and observables when predicting outcome variables.  Empirical evidence suggests this new method incorporates less outcome variance into the treatment variable compared to outcome modeling alone, thereby improving its efficiency.  Empirical tests confirm that our proposed method incorporates less variance compared to baseline estimators that only rely on outcome modeling.  Empirical tests confirm that our proposed method paired with outcome modeling orthogonality conditions achieves better efficiency than baseline estimators.  Empirical tests confirm that our proposed method has comparable performance to double robust estimators.  Empirical tests confirm that our proposed method has comparable efficiency loss to outcome modeling alone in scenarios without outcome modeling misspecification

The role of $\tau$ is taking center stage in the current research into lepton flavor universality violations in B-physics, warranting greater theoretical attention in the coming years. Enhanced data samples from Belle-II, as well as LHCb, ATLAS, and CMS, will be crucial in further investigating the anomaly. We outline several key problems in theoretical lattice QCD that need to be resolved in order to determine whether new physics beyond the Standard Model exists, as well as the most difficult forecasting tasks for experiments to complete in the years ahead.

A tabletop-sized rotating annulus setup has been extensively studied to mimic the general circulation of mid-latitude atmospheric circulation. The device effectively replicates two crucial factors influencing large-scale air circulation: the rotation of the Earth and the temperature variations between the equator and poles. While numerous studies have been conducted in the past on this setup, most have been limited to specific configurations of rotation rates and temperature variations, resulting in observations of distinct flow patterns and behaviors. To address this limitation, a comprehensive dataset of 48 experiments was analyzed using diverse combinations of rotation rates and thermal conditions. The experiments were compared with results from 48 corresponding numerical simulations to establish relationships between the experiment parameters and observable features of the flow patterns, such as the average number of waves, meridional velocity differences, and critical Taylor number values. The study identified two non-dimensional parameters that characterize the experiment conditions and influence wave dynamics in the setup. One parameter, representing the relative rotation of the inner and outer cylinders, affects both the wave behavior and the formation of specific flow patterns. A second parameter, representing the ratio of vertical to horizontal thermal gradients, mainly affects the structure of the wave patterns but is less influential in other aspects. The study discovered that in setups with closely matched rotation rates, a particular temperature difference between the equator and poles promotes the formation of intense storms, whereas a significant equator-to-pole temperature difference promotes a more balanced distribution of storm intensity.

A typical technique in Bayesian extreme value theory involves modelling threshold exceedances using a parametric model, often modelling exceedances as a threshold exceedance count with parameters estimated using threshold values. These threshold values are then treated as changeless in order to obtain a model that can be used for inference. However, selecting an appropriate threshold value can significantly impact the model's fit below threshold values, requiring the threshold value to be determined prior to inference. A new Bayesian technique is proposed for obtaining model parameters and threshold values simultaneously, modelling the exceedance exceedance process below threshold values as a threshold-dependent Poisson process. This results in the model's threshold excess counts following independent Poisson distributions whose parameters depend on the threshold value. This results in the model's threshold value following independent Poisson distributions whose parameters depend on the threshold value. This results in the model's threshold value following independent Poisson distributions whose parameters depend on the threshold value.

In offline reinforcement learning, we aim to develop data-efficient policies that achieve optimal results, given a predetermined set of observations. In practical applications, however, the training datasets are often contaminated with noisy or irrelevant samples, which can compromise the performance and security of the learned policies. To address this issue, we propose an offline learning framework that is resistant to data corruption. Our framework involves two main components: first, we divide the available data into a searchable dataset, which encompasses every available sample, and an identifiable dataset, from which the true samples can be distinguished; second, we use the samples in the identifiable data to train an estimator of a specific probability distribution, known as the behavior distribution, and then employ this estimator to develop data-efficient policies that draw training samples solely from the searchable dataset. To evaluate our method, we consider four commonly used loss functions in reinforcement learning, prove its robustness properties, and demonstrate its practical effectiveness on synthetic and real-world corrupted datasets.

This study demonstrates a logarithmic convexity linked to observability at a specific point in time for the one-dimensional heat equation under dynamic boundary conditions, leading to impulse approximate controllability in similar scenarios with dynamic boundaries. Additionally, we provide a detailed estimate for the cost of impulse control. Our research includes a step-by-step procedure for finding the impulsive control of minimal L^2-norm and supports these findings with numerical tests to verify the efficiency of the developed algorithm.

A consensus has not been established on the definition and optimal detection methods for out-of-distribution examples despite general agreement on their importance. We identified distinct behaviors of two major detection methods - model calibration and density estimation - in response to background and semantic shifts in data, which were found across various language understanding datasets. In our evaluation, density estimation outperformed model calibration in background shift scenarios but struggled with semantic shifts, with both approaches underperforming when confronted with challenge data, underscoring a need for clearer definitions in method comparison.

In recent years, the development of brownian molecular machines powered by electric current has been accelerated by the discovery of their potential applications. Despite several theoretical and experimental studies conducted over the past decade, creating efficient molecular machines remains an unresolved issue. Many questions remain to be answered to clarify their operational limits. In this study, a theoretical model is developed to describe a brownian molecular machine powered by electric current, using simple quantum tunneling as a driving force. It is demonstrated that electric current can be generated to drive the machine, however, it simultaneously slows down and is consumed, thereby limiting its utility. It is found that three-state machines, unlike two-state machines, can function efficiently, however, they require more complex chemical reactions, making their realization more challenging.

Building on a 2014 framework, researchers introduced various interpretations of transducer behavior, including one-way resynchronizability, which means that for every input string there is only one point where processing occurs simultaneously between both processors. This concept has proven challenging to work with theoretically due to its limitations. Consequently, a weaker form was introduced, which allows for processing occurrences of particular letter sequences to be considered simultaneous. This exploration focuses on characterizing this more manageable concept for specific types of transducers, including those with constant or unbounded 'loops'. Although some successful characterizations have been achieved, many important questions remain unresolved, including the relationship between different forms of one-way resynchronizability.

In this study, we examine the conventional convolution operation between a image and a filter, as well as its high-dimensional generalizations. By exploiting connections to the discrete Fourier transform, we achieve significant speedup on standard computers, achieving a time complexity of $\tilde O(N^{2.687})$, and also provide a solution for the 'near field' case with a complexity of $\tilde O(d^2n^{2.687})$. Furthermore, for transformations based on graph signals, we propose an efficient algorithm running in $\tilde O\Big(\frac{d^2n^{\frac{5}{3}}}{\log n}\Big)$.

The discovery of T-dwarf GJ 229B in 1995 offered initial insights into its composition, but a comprehensive analysis with current spectroscopic techniques has since been lacking. Recent research estimates its mass and age at 70 M_J and 800 Myr respectively, leveraging existing flux estimates and theoretical models of atmospheric development. Although previous studies attempted to obtain emission spectra, their results were inconclusive due to variations in measurement techniques. With a novel approach utilizing public data from the IRSA database, an accurate high-resolution spectrum of GJ 229B has now been assembled, facilitating an advanced chemical composition analysis using the APOLLO code. This study confirms previously assumed values of 2.0 times solar metallicity and +2.0 expected excess [C/ O], and reveals a chaotic atmospheric environment characterized by dynamic weather patterns.

To search for the potential existence of the unique $0^{--}$ state, we created a systematic approach to constructing hadronic wave functions with the $0^{--}$ quantum numbers, considering the effects of color-magnetic interactions. Our calculations indicate that the mass of the purely gluonic $0^{--}$ state is $3.01$ GeV, while the mass of a hybrid state made up of a quark pair and a gluon is $2.75$ GeV, and the mass of a state composed of five quarks is $2.71$ GeV. Additionally, we found that the quark-$g$ state with the same $J^{PC}$ has the lowest mass at $2.47$ GeV, and its coupling is strong enough ($21.1$ MeV) to potentially be detected experimentally through the decays $J/\psi \to \pi^+ \pi^- X$ and $J/\psi \to K^+ K^- X$, where $X$ represents the lightest exotic state. Calculations also revealed that the quark-gluon state has the lowest hadronic mass at $1.42$ GeV, and its large coupling ($20$ MeV) suggests it may contribute significantly ($10\%$) to a previously unexplained enhancement near threshold in the $J^{PC}=0^{--}$ channel that may have been detected via $e

A comprehensive review of the LHCb results regarding $B_s$ oscillation and $\Delta\Gamma_s$ mixting ratio measurements is provided, along with an examination of these findings in comparison to theoretical predictions made by different lattice QCD models.

Airborne transmission risks in confined environments like buses are largely unknown due to a lack of data. This study fills this gap by measuring and comparing the migration of viruses in a bus to theoretical well-mixed conditions. Experiments were conducted to simulate the spread of viruses using tracers in a moving bus and simulate both well-mixed and stratified airflow. The results showed significant differences between the spread patterns of volatile and non-volatile substances, highlighting the importance of considering environmental factors like temperature and humidity in influenza virus survival. Although there were differences, it was found that well-mixed models provide a more accurate representation of the influenza virus's potential spread over long durations, supporting their use in disease transmission studies in urban buses.

This study has conducted large-scale shell-model computations for $ eta$-decay attributes. Researchers at ILL, Grenoble, recently performed $ eta$-delayed $\gamma$-ray spectroscopy to investigate $ eta$-decay properties related to the $^{137}$Te ($J^\pi=11/2^-$) to $^{137}$I ($J^\pi=9/2^-$) transition. We conducted shell-model calculations for both the parent ($^{135,137}$Te with $J^\pi=11/2^-$) and daughter nuclei ($^{135}$I ($J^\pi=10$) and $^{137}$I ($J^\pi=9/2^-$)). Calculations were carried out with the conventional shell-model code for the nucleon configuration.
